Plot a Sigma Profile

Source: R/profile_sigma.R
plot.sigma_profile.Rd

Draws one panel per covariate from a profile_sigma() result. Each panel plots AICc or the log-likelihood (whichever metric was chosen in profile_sigma()) against sigma, with points at the evaluated values and a dashed red vertical line at the estimated sigma.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sigma_profile'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A sigma_profile object from profile_sigma().

...

Not used.

Value

A named list of ggplot objects, one per covariate, returned invisibly. Each plot is printed as a side effect. Modify a stored plot and print it again to customize it.

Details

How to read the plot. The x-axis is sigma in map units, and the y-axis is AICc (lower is better) or the log-likelihood (higher is better). A clear trough in AICc, or peak in log-likelihood, at the dashed line means the data identify the scale of effect well. A flat curve means many scales fit about equally well. Points are joined with straight lines, so a hard-radius covariate's stepped likelihood is not shown between grid values. See profile_sigma() for how the values are computed.

See also

profile_sigma()

Examples

## A stored profile from the Quick Start fit (two covariates, 15 values each)
prof <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "cache-quickstart.rds",
                            package = "multiScaleR"))$prof
# One AICc panel each for land1 and land2. AICc is lowest near the
# estimated sigma (dashed line)
p <- plot(prof)



# The stored ggplot objects can be modified and drawn again
p$land1 + ggplot2::labs(x = "sigma (m)")
